terms.latin: culpam in sē recipere / culpam agnōscere
terms.comment: These imply more than neutral answerability.

terms.gloss: enter in the account, reckon, charge; put down to someone as a merit or a fault
evidence: Col. 1.7: vīlicī servī longē plūs imputant sēminis jactī quam quod sēverint (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Not found before the Augustan age (Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: gaudent mūneribus, sed nec data imputant nec acceptīs obligantur
phrases.english: they delight in gifts, but they neither count what they have given as a claim nor feel bound by what they receive

sources: Lewis & Short: imputo · Lewis & Short: agnosco
